title: Coral and the Garden
premise: Jude Winterbourne, last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, has spent a decade hiding her gift among the ledgers of the Meridian Guild, which trades in impossible things. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands—a map to the Garden where swordspeakers were made and unmade—Jude learns the Guild's masters intend to harvest it and resurrect the war her oaths ended. Hunted by her own employers and shadowed by a rival who knows her name, Jude must choose between the loyalty she swore and the truth she carries, culminating at the Garden's heart where she can either destroy the source of swordspeech forever or claim its power herself. She burns the Garden, losing her gift but keeping her self, and rebuilds the Guild on honest ledgers.
about_author: Ada Kavanagh is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people who keep records of things that should never have happened. She lives near the coast, where she collects sea glass and insists the tides keep better secrets than any guild.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the Meridian Guild's counting-house, Jude balances ledgers of impossible trades—a bottled storm, a borrowed year—while concealing the sword-speech humming under her skin. A routine audit reveals a payment made in a currency that hasn't existed since the war. Emotional beat: the ache of a gifted life spent pretending to be ordinary.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A bleeding courier collapses against the Guild's back entrance at closing bell, pressing a wax-sealed map into Jude's hands and gasping her true surname—Winterbourne—before dying. Guild enforcers approach. Emotional beat: terror as invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude hides the map inside a ledger of debts and lies smoothly to Master Corvane, the Guild's silver-tongued auditor, about the courier. Corvane's too-long pause suggests he doesn't believe her. Emotional beat: first taste of deception as survival.

chapters.title: The Map That Breathes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, alone at night. The map unrolls itself, ink crawling into new shapes: a route through the Drowned Marches to a place marked only by a blooming rose of thorns—the Garden. Her sword-speech resonates with the parchment. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Oath Cost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's POV. Ten years earlier: the last stand at Ashfall Bridge, where the swordspeakers were broken and Jude's mentor made her swear silence in exchange for survival. Emotional beat: grief reframed as the reason she hides.

chapters.title: The Rival Who Knows
chapters.summary: Sefa Ilvane's POV. Sefa, a Guild factor and former war-child, recognizes Jude's tell when she lies. She reports nothing—yet—because she wants something bigger than Jude: the map itself. Emotional beat: predatory patience.

chapters.title: Debts Called In
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corvane summons Jude: the courier's death has been logged as robbery, and the 'stolen' goods are described in detail she never reported. The Guild knows she has the map. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Running the Tidewalks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude flees the counting-house through the city's flooded lower streets, using a swordspeaker's trick—speaking a locked gate open—for the first time in a decade. Sefa sees. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: An Offer in the Rain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa catches Jude in a rainmarket and offers partnership instead of betrayal: Sefa knows the Marches, Jude holds the map, and both distrust Corvane. Emotional beat: wary, transactional trust.

chapters.title: The Drowned Marches
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The pair enters the sunken country where the old war was fought—petrified soldiers still standing in the marshes, their swords rusted mid-swing. Jude hears the dead weapons whisper. Emotional beat: dread and history's weight.

chapters.title: Whispers in Rust
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The petrified swords respond to Jude's blood, briefly animating and nearly killing Sefa before Jude speaks them down. Sefa now knows what Jude is. Emotional beat: the secret she kept is out, and it's monstrous.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A ferryman demands payment in memories. Sefa pays a memory of her brother; Jude pays the memory of her mentor's face. Emotional beat: what each woman values, revealed by what she surrenders.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hounds
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Guild's auditor dispatches the Hollow Men—mercenaries with their names surgically forgotten—ordering them to retrieve the map and leave no witnesses. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: The Inn at Halfway
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At a fortified inn, Jude and Sefa rest, and Sefa reveals her history: her village fed the Garden's first harvest. The Hollow Men arrive at dusk. Emotional beat: fragile intimacy before violence.

chapters.title: Blades Without Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, action chapter. Jude speaks a dead soldier's sword back to life to fight the Hollow Men, breaking her oath's letter if not its spirit. They escape, but the sword remembers her. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of power reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Sword Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The reanimated sword follows Jude, loyal as a hound, whispering fragments of its last wielder's memories—including the location of a hidden swordspeaker cache. Emotional beat: being known by something she made.

chapters.title: Thornwall
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The pair crosses Thornwall, a hedge of living brambles that tests intruders with visions of their deepest want. Sefa sees herself ruling; Jude sees only an empty ledger and peace. Emotional beat: desire made visible.

chapters.title: The Garden's Outer Court
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the Garden: a vast terraced estate where swordspeech was cultivated, now overgrown and guarded by topiary golems still bound to old commands. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Grave
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In a crypt they find the Garden's maker, buried upright with a final inscription: 'I grew power; it grew me. Burn what I planted.' Jude begins to understand what the map's courier died for. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane reaches the Garden with the Hollow Men, revealing he isn't Guild at all—he's a remnant of the old enemy order, and the Guild was his ledger all along. Emotional beat: the betrayal behind the betrayal.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The golems, bound by older law than loyalty, seize Jude and Sefa and deliver them to Corvane. Sefa bargains: her knowledge of the Garden's irrigation of power for her life. Jude is taken below. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Imprisoned in the Garden's root-vault, Jude finds the source: a tree grown from the first swordspeaker, its roots drinking oaths. Corvane plans to graft himself onto it and reignite the war under Guild banners. Emotional beat: horror at power's true price.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Above, Sefa sabotages the Hollow Men's anchor-chains, choosing Jude and truth over her bargain. She is wounded and captured. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at cost.

chapters.title: The Tree That Eats Oaths
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The tree speaks to Jude in her mentor's voice, offering restoration of everything the oath took—her order, her name, her gift—in exchange for becoming its new root-keeper. Emotional beat: temptation aimed at her deepest wound.

chapters.title: The Hollow Men Break
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa turns the captured Hollow Men by reminding them they once had names; one, Brac, remembers his and turns on Corvane. Emotional beat: identity as weapon and salvation.

chapters.title: Graft
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane begins the grafting rite, and the Garden convulses—every sword in the world hums, and in distant cities, blades rise from sheaths. Emotional beat: the war restarting in real time.

chapters.title: The Rising Blades
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude escapes her cell as the vault floods with awakened swords, the reanimated hound-sword cutting her free. She fights upward through a garden gone to war with itself. Emotional beat: chaos as consequence.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Trellis
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude reaches the grafting trellis and duels Corvane, half-grafted, his speech now a chorus of stolen voices. She loses her sword and wins by speaking the tree's oldest command: 'Grow toward the sun.' Emotional beat: victory through surrender of force.

chapters.title: What Corvane Wanted
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV, dying. Ungrafted and mortal again, Corvane confesses he only wanted to matter in a ledger that had forgotten him. He gives Jude the Guild's master seal. Emotional beat: pity for the corrupted.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude sets the Garden alight, and the tree's last gift is a choice: keep her swordspeech by taking root, or stay human and let the gift die with the Garden. Emotional beat: the climax's true cost.

chapters.title: Ashfall Again
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude walks out of the burning Garden human, her gift gone, carrying Sefa on her back. Behind them, the war's potential dies in smoke. Emotional beat: grief and relief braided together.

chapters.title: The Long Road Home
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The journey back through the Marches, past petrified soldiers who now crumble peacefully. Brac and the freed Hollow Men travel as escort. Emotional beat: quiet aftermath, unlikely company.

chapters.title: The Guild Reckons
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Returning to the city, Jude presents the master seal and the evidence of Corvane's fraud to the Guild's council, demanding honest ledgers. Some masters resist; the factors—led by rumor of Sefa's deeds—do not. Emotional beat: power reclaimed without corruption.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Possible Things
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Guild reopens under new rules: it trades in difficult things, not impossible ones. Jude takes the auditor's desk, keeping accounts she can defend. Emotional beat: rebuilding as penance and hope.

chapters.title: The Sword's Farewell
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The hound-sword, its purpose ended, asks to be unmade. Jude speaks it back to rust and buries it with the courier who started everything, whose name she finally learns. Emotional beat: mourning the last piece of her old self.

chapters.title: A Visitor from the Marches
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A young girl arrives at the Guild with a humming kitchen knife and no idea why. Jude recognizes the gift surviving in small, scattered ways. Emotional beat: the past refusing to be fully buried—and a choice about what to do with it.

chapters.title: Teaching Without Oaths
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Instead of an oath of silence, Jude offers the girl an apprenticeship: learn the gift, learn its cost, keep honest records. Sefa warns it's dangerous. Jude answers that secrets were the danger. Emotional beat: breaking the cycle.

chapters.title: The Garden in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa files the Garden's true history in the Guild's public archive—the first impossible thing recorded honestly. Scholars and survivors begin to arrive. Emotional beat: truth as the only durable foundation.

chapters.title: Salt and Roses
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A year later: the counting-house at dusk, the girl practicing scales of speech in the yard, Sefa arguing over accounts, sea air through open windows. Jude writes the final entry in her own ledger and signs her full name. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.

chapters.title: Coda: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, brief final chapter. In the Drowned Marches, where the Garden burned, a single thornless rose blooms from the ash—power's residue, harmless, beautiful, watched. Jude, visiting, leaves it uncut. Emotional beat: hope tempered by vigilance; the theme resolved in an image.
